content: Aristoteles (384–322 BCE) was an ancient Greek philosopher—student of Plato and tutor to Alexander the Great—who founded the Lyceum and produced foundational works on logic, metaphysics, ethics, politics, rhetoric, poetics, and the natural sciences that shaped Western thought for millennia.
